messages:
sara: Quick sync — idea: add a lightweight runtime handoff validation harness to the model onboarding flow. not a full bench, just three quick signals before we mark a model as 'runtime-ready'.

sara: Proposed checks:
- determinism smoke: run N small seeded forwards and compare token-level outputs (tolerance for non-deterministic ops)
- perf snapshot: p50/p95 per-token latency for 4 common seq lengths (8/64/256/1024) on the target inf node
- semantic drift: embedding dist to golden outputs on 200 golden prompts (fast approximate)

matt: can we catch quantized ABI/ordering regressions here? those are the nasty silent ones.

priya: +1. also add a model-surface schema check (inputs/attention_mask/kv cache shape & dtype). i've seen runtime errors where the proto changed and nobody noticed.

olivia: clarification — this is different from the onboarding bench we run for acceptance, right? this should be the quick handoff that infra runs to accept a model into the serving pool.

sara: correct. think of it as the "handoff gate" between eng-ml and runtime: fast (~30s-2m), deterministic-ish, actionable failure reasons. not exhaustive.

matt: for determinism smoke, how strict? full token equality will fail for fp16+quant combos. we should use a configurable tolerance / normalized edit-distance or top-k token set overlap.

priya: agree. suggest three tiers: exact (for fp32), fuzzy (edit distance < X) and semsim (embedding cosine > 0.97). default to fuzzy for any quantized binaries. we can infer tier from model metadata.

olivia: perf snapshot needs to be reproducible: pin CPU/GPU affinity, batching=1, and a fixed prompt mix. otherwise noisy. also capture KV-cache correctness by replaying a multi-chunk prompt and ensuring continuity.

matt: noted. i'll draft a small perf runner that emits p50/p95/P99 and a tiny histogram. output should be machine-parseable for the console.

priya: i'll own schema + golden-output artifacts. for golden outputs we'll store compressed embeddings and a small set of canonical prompts per model family. compare via approximate nearest neighbor (faiss/onnx).

infra-bot: deploy-check: handoff-harness v0.1 is available on staging: https://ci/internal/artifacts/handoff-harness/0.1 :white_check_mark:

olivia: nice. we also need clear failure codes so runtime can auto-reject vs auto-queue for human review. e.g. CODE_SCHEMA, CODE_PERF_REGRESS, CODE_DRIFT_HIGH, CODE_TIMEOUT.

sara: love the failure codes idea. let's make failure payload include: code, short msg, suggested next step, diagnostic artifacts (logs, sample outputs, perf traces).

matt: timeline? i can get a perf runner PR by EOW if someone else wires the CI job and failure codes.

priya: i'll prepare the schema checks + golden prompt packs and a small script to produce compressed embeddings by Thursday.

olivia: i'll own the docs page describing the gate semantics, thresholds, and the "what to do if X fails" runbook. will draft today.

sara: owners: matt (perf runner), priya (schema & golden artifacts), olivia (docs & runbook). i'll create the repo eng-ml/handoff-harness and a checklist issue linking these.

sara: quick example command we can expose for local runs:
```
./run_handoff_check --model-id rwd-xyz --seed 42 --samples 20 --target-node staging-rt-1
```

priya: tiny nit — add --quant-tier auto so it selects fuzzy vs exact behavior based on model metadata.

matt: will add a --dump-trace flag to collect perf traces for failed runs.

olivia: and i'll add the failure-code table to the docs.

sara: perfect. if no objections i'll open the repo + issue now and ping owners. thanks all :thumbsup:
